public_sources.title: Batch Invariance - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Official current documentation: batch invariance is beta, uses deterministic kernels/behavior independent of batch size/order, requires supported NVIDIA hardware, disables some nondeterministic optimizations, and may reduce performance.

public_sources.title: Reproducibility - vLLM
public_sources.relevance: Official reproducibility boundary: not guaranteed by default; online mode needs batch invariance; even then reproducibility is scoped to same hardware and vLLM version.

public_sources.title: Reproducibility - PyTorch 2.13
public_sources.relevance: Official warning that complete reproducibility is not guaranteed across releases/platforms even with identical seeds and that deterministic operations can be slower.

public_sources.title: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation
public_sources.relevance: Primary systems evidence that LLM nondeterminism comes from batching/reduction order and that verify-rollback can provide selective determinism. Their SGLang deterministic baseline lost 24-36% throughput in tested offline workloads; selective LLM-42 substantially recovered throughput.

public_sources.title: CoRun: Padding is Simple and Efficient for Deterministic LLM Inference
public_sources.relevance: Very recent primary evidence that batch-invariant deterministic kernels can cost >2x latency and up to 74% throughput in tested systems, while a fixed-shape scheduling design recovered much of that overhead. Used to motivate measuring the exact determinism tax rather than assuming it is small.

public_sources.title: Anytime-Valid Inference Under Outcome Delay: A Design-Based Approach
public_sources.relevance: Primary statistical evidence that outcome timing can be informative and that the filtration is central; supports the requirement for a richer timing model if stochastic fastest-completion data are used inferentially.

determinism_certification_gate.purpose: First-completion hedging is admitted as identity-preserving only if the execution stack can certify that every physical replica realizes the same frozen logical attempt. Otherwise the duplicate is a new stochastic sample and fastest selection is forbidden under the marginal paired-sign null.
static_fingerprint: GPU architecture and supported deterministic domain
sampling algorithm and complete sampling parameters
seed plus explicit per-request RNG/random-tape identity where available
batch-invariance/deterministic flags and any all-reduce restrictions
determinism_certification_gate.preflight: Before enabling a replica class, run a fixed prompt x seed matrix across the intended replica placements, batch sizes/orders, concurrency levels and scheduling perturbations. Compare token IDs and, when decision-relevant, logprobs/structured outputs. Zero mismatch is required inside the certified domain, but finite preflight is evidence, not a mathematical proof of global determinism.
determinism_certification_gate.runtime: Each hedge carries logical_attempt_id and deterministic_fingerprint. A replica with a different fingerprint cannot satisfy the same-attempt contract. Prefer execution modes that verify determinism per request (e.g. fixed-shape/batch-invariant or verify-rollback semantics) rather than assuming a seed is sufficient.
determinism_certification_gate.fail_closed: Any detected replica disagreement or fingerprint drift invalidates identity-preserving hedging for that logical attempt. Do not choose the fastest divergent output. Use a canonical replica fixed before timing, if the protocol explicitly allows it, or return unresolved/quarantine and require recertification.
determinism_certification_gate.scope: This gate is a proposed evaluation protocol. Public framework/paper results establish feasible deterministic mechanisms and their limits, not that a particular deployment is certified.

determinism_tax_break_even.model: Let d be the multiplicative latency slowdown caused by deterministic execution relative to the original non-deterministic single-attempt latency distribution. Multiply the prior checkpoint's synthetic hedge latency ratios by d. This is a sensitivity calculation, not a claim that real deterministic overhead is a pure scalar.
determinism_tax_break_even.interpretation: A deterministic mode can erase conservative hedge gains even when statistical validity is restored. In the synthetic heavy-tail model, aggressive three-way identity replication retains p95 benefit under a much larger determinism slowdown than a p90/p95 delayed hedge, but its full launched obligation is much higher. Real choice requires measured deterministic-mode p50/p95/p99 and actual cancellation/billing, not throughput alone.

timing_no_free_lunch_for_stochastic_fast.setup: Launch m iid stochastic attempts with sign S~Bernoulli(q) and arbitrary conditional latency distribution T|S. The scientific target remains the single-attempt marginal q. Only the fastest sign is retained; slower attempts may be canceled.
timing_no_free_lunch_for_stochastic_fast.null_range: Under H0 q<=1/2 and otherwise unrestricted T|S, the fastest plus probability can be as low as q^m (make plus always slower) or as high as 1-(1-q)^m (make plus always faster). At the boundary q=1/2 this range is [2^-m, 1-2^-m]; for m=3 it is [0.125,0.875].
timing_no_free_lunch_for_stochastic_fast.alternative_overlap: For q=0.60 and m=3 the corresponding attainable range is [0.216,0.936], which massively overlaps the exact-null range. Thus fastest-sign data alone cannot uniformly distinguish a modest q>1/2 alternative from the marginal null when sign-latency dependence is unrestricted.
timing_no_free_lunch_for_stochastic_fast.conclusion: There is no distribution-free free lunch from fastest stochastic replicas for the original marginal-q test. To use first-completion evidence with power, one must add a valid model/bound for sign-latency dependence, observe nonselected outcomes, randomize a design with known inclusion probabilities, or explicitly change the estimand to latency-aware utility.
timing_no_free_lunch_for_stochastic_fast.robust_evalue_note: One could build an e-factor against the worst-case null fastest-plus bound 1-2^-m, but that null is so permissive that moderate single-attempt improvements may have little or no uniform power. This is not a substitute for an identity-preserving replica contract.
timing_no_free_lunch_for_stochastic_fast.scope: The exact range statement concerns iid Bernoulli signs with arbitrary sign-conditional latency and fastest-sign-only observation. Richer side information or constrained latency models can tighten the null.

estimand_separation.single_attempt_quality: If the target is eventual quality of one stochastic model attempt, independent hedges selected by completion order are selection-biased under unrestricted outcome-timing dependence.
estimand_separation.ensemble_quality: A completion-order-independent majority/aggregate can be valid but evaluates an ensemble policy with a different response distribution.
estimand_separation.latency_aware_utility: If deployment utility is explicitly defined as first valid response quality by time t, fastest completion can be part of the estimand rather than a nuisance. Such a metric must be reported separately from single-attempt quality and needs its own valid comparison design.

new_measurement_validity_rules: Do not treat determinism as a binary seed flag. Certify a bounded runtime/hardware/model/sampler domain and record the exact deterministic fingerprint with every logical attempt.
Benchmark the determinism tax before deciding that deterministic hedging is an optimization. The validity fix can cost enough latency/throughput to erase the tail benefit.

Under the marginal sign null with unrestricted sign-latency dependence, fastest stochastic replicas are not merely a slightly biased estimator; their observable plus rate can range from 2^-m to 1-2^-m at q=1/2. A timing model/conditional null is required for informative first-completion inference.
Keep three estimands separate: single stochastic attempt, predeclared ensemble/aggregate, and latency-aware first-response utility. Do not move evidence among them without an explicit mapping.
A deterministic replica mismatch is an inference event, not only an operations bug: fastest selection must fail closed because the same-attempt proof is gone.
scope_guards: The determinism overhead figures from LLM-42 and CoRun are tied to their tested systems/models/hardware and cannot be translated directly into a universal latency multiplier d.
The break-even table is a sensitivity transform of the previous worker-local heavy-tail simulation; it is not a benchmark of vLLM, SGLang, LLM-42, CoRun, any API, or any provider.

The fastest-sign null range permits arbitrary T|S and therefore is deliberately worst-case. With independently validated structural constraints on latency/outcome dependence, sharper inference may be possible.
Finite conformance testing cannot prove determinism outside the tested fingerprint/domain; production admission needs both a runtime contract and ongoing mismatch monitoring.

frontier.action: Derive a fail-closed deterministic-hedging admission test that includes deterministic fingerprint drift and an upper confidence bound on observed replica mismatch rate from a disjoint conformance set. Decide what evidence is enough to enable fastest physical replica while avoiding a false claim of mathematical equivalence.

Derive timing-aware inference for genuinely stochastic replicas under an explicit, independently calibrated bound on P(+ | completion-time/covariates, past), and compare its power with the worst-case fastest-plus null bound and canonical single-attempt evaluation.

Model selective-determinism systems (verified speculation/fixed-shape scheduling) with measured p50/p95/p99 overhead rather than a scalar d, then re-optimize hedge delay and replica count under wall/full-obligation/effective-compute objectives.
Define and test a separate latency-aware utility estimand for deployment where first valid completion is the object of interest; keep it orthogonal to single-attempt quality certification.

exact_next_action: Build a statistically honest determinism admission rule: use an independent conformance corpus to upper-bound replica mismatch probability within a frozen runtime fingerprint, combine that bound with the consequence of a rare mismatch for fastest-selection validity, and determine whether any nonzero mismatch rate can be tolerated without reverting to canonical-attempt or timing-aware inference.
